content.title: City Council's Work
content.summary: The City Council's Strategic Plan for 2024-2030 serves as a foundational document for addressing community needs and integrates the operating and capital budgets to guide daily operations across five priority areas. Developed in response to evolving challenges, including the COVID-19 pandemic, the plan emphasizes alignment with the City Council's vision through measurable goals and regular progress reporting. Additionally, the City maintains a Legislative Agenda to monitor and influence state and federal legislation affecting local governance, prioritizing local control and the preservation of municipal authority.
content.body:
## City Council Strategic Plan

View the [City Council Strategic Plan 2024 to 2030](/DocumentCenter/View/4218/COA-Council-Strat-Plan-2024-ADA---facing-pages-1).

### A Foundation for Meeting Community Needs

The City Council Strategic Plan is the City's guiding document and foundation for meeting current and future community needs. It integrates the Biennial Operating and the Capital Improvement Budgets, and subsequently drives daily operations within the City across five Work Systems. The strategic plan identifies results, prioritizes change and addresses resource allocation. It has a six-year time horizon, bolstered by an annual iterative review considering shorter-term adjustments, and a 10-year outlook to incorporate long-range initiatives reflected in the financial plan.

### Background

In 2013, the Arvada City Council adopted its first comprehensive Strategic Plan, focusing on five priority areas: Safe Community, Infrastructure, Community and Economic Development, Vibrant Community and Neighborhoods, and Organizational and Service Effectiveness. These areas, known as Work Systems, promote collaboration in service delivery.

The 2020-2025 Strategic Plan, adopted in 2019, saw significant changes between 2020 and 2024 due to the evolving environment, particularly the COVID-19 pandemic. These updates allowed the City to remain adaptive and responsive, emphasizing short-term goals over long-term vision.

In early 2024, the City Council, in collaboration with City Leadership, began developing the 2024-2030 Strategic Plan to create a more visionary and aligned strategy, supporting the City’s mission to deliver superior services to enhance the lives of everyone in our community. On May 20, 2024, City Council adopted the 2024-2030 Strategic Plan.

### Strategic Alignment and Measuring Progress

The City Council's Strategic Plan (CCSP) is designed to provide a high-level outcome-focused direction from City Council. The Plan creates the opportunity for City Teams to align their work to the City Council strategic vision and results. The City will track this alignment in Internal Implementation Plans (IIP), including specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and timely (SMART) goals that detail the annual actions that need to be taken to progress the Plan. The SMART goals will be accompanied by performance measures that provide quantitative indicators to communicate and inform the direction and successful completion of these goals. Together they serve as an important form of accountability to the City Council and to the public.

Every quarter, directors will report out to the City Manager’s Office on the progress of their implementation plans. Periodic Strategic Plan updates to City Council will be provided through City Council Meetings, Quarterly Financial Reports, Quarterly Implementation Plan Reports, and an Annual City Manager status report.

To view the CCSP, including strategic results, goals and performance measures, visit [the Strategic Alignment webpage](https://www.arvadaco.gov/241/Strategic-Alignment).

## Legislative Agenda

The City of Arvada actively monitors legislation from other levels of government that may affect the City and our community. The City's Legislative Agenda outlines the City Council's position on potential State of Colorado legislation, and serves as a reference for the state legislative delegations, the City team and members of the community.

The City's position on legislation at the state and federal level is based on the following principles:

- Maintain Local Control and Home Rule: Decisions impacting Arvadans are best undertaken by the government that is closest to the electorate, the Arvada City Council.
- No Mandates: Mandates from other levels of government, especially unfunded, should not be imposed on local government.
- Preservation of Traditional Authority: The traditional authority and powers of municipal government in areas such as land use and zoning, and sales tax, should not be further eroded.
- Local Problems Need Local Solutions: Statewide solutions to local issues often have unintended consequences on municipalities and should be avoided.

View the [Legislative Agenda](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/munidocs/munidocs?nodeId=8e150371f661b). You may also view the [Legislative Tracker site](https://statebillinfo.com/SBI/index.cfm?fuseaction=Public.Dossier&id=37757&pk=772&style=pinstripe) for up-to-date bill tracking information.

## Committee Assignments

Each Councilmember represents the City of Arvada on various committees, boards, and task forces within Arvada and the region.
